q: 1. The contractor is responsible for
options: procuring material which is not supplied by the owner
organizing and planning the work as per drawing
executing the work as per specifications laid down in the contract
explain: A contractor's overall responsibility covers material procurement (where not owner-supplied), planning, and execution per specifications - all of the above.

q: 2. In the analysis of rate, the profit for the contractor is generally taken as
explain: In standard rate analysis practice, contractor's profit margin is conventionally taken as 15% of the cost.

q: 3. Mobilization advance up to 10% of the cost of work is given to a contractor
options: on commencement of work at site for payment of loan taken by him
for the purchase of construction materials
for the payment of advances to labour and other staff
for all activities required to start the work at site on finalization of the contract document
explain: Mobilization advance covers all start-up activities needed to begin work after the contract is finalised.

q: 4. Security deposit deducted at 5% from contractor's bills is
options: refunded when the contractor has completed the work
refunded even before the completion of the work provided good progress has been established
retained till the expected life of the structure of say 100 years and spent for maintenance
refunded when the defect liability period of six months or one monsoon whichever is later is over
explain: The deposit is released only after the defect liability period ends.

q: 5. If a contractor is found corrupt for tender work, then what should be done by concerned office?
explain: Per the answer key, his tender is cancelled.

q: 6. Which of the following documents should be prepared and submitted by a contractor?
explain: The bid document is prepared and submitted by the contractor in response to a tender notice.

q: 7. In QCBS method of procurement, evaluation of consulting firms to award the contract, the weightage will be
explain: Per the answer key, 80% technical and 20% financial.

q: 8. Direct purchase can be done for procurement of consulting services or construction works upto
options: 5 lakh in case of consulting services
5 lakh in case of construction works
explain: Per the answer key, both limits apply.

q: 9. Pre-tender stage requires
options: selection of site and acquisition of land
finalisation of designs and preparation of estimate
explain: Before a tender is called, the owner must secure the site, finalize the design, and prepare a cost estimate to ensure the project is ready for bidding.

q: 10. During construction, price variation clause in a contract applies to:
options: increase in cost of important materials only
variation in the cost of materials, labour and fuel
variation in total cost of the project estimated and a lump-sum figure
explain: Price variation clauses cover changes in the cost of materials, labour, and fuel (POL) elements during construction execution.

q: 11. For the ICB procurement method, the period of bidding to contractor must be at least
explain: Per the answer key, 45 days.

q: 12. Site order book is used for recording
options: indents for materials to be ordered
explain: It records the engineer's instructions to the contractor.

q: 13. The amount of earnest money generally deposited at the time of submission of tender is
explain: Earnest money deposit (bid security) is typically fixed at 2% to 3% of the estimated project cost[cite: 1].

q: 14. The amount of earnest money generally deposited at the time of submission of tender is
explain: In Nepal's Public Procurement Act, bid security (earnest money) is usually 2% to 3% of the estimated amount.

q: 15. By using the method of sealed quotation, which of the following cannot procured?
options: all of the above can be procured
explain: The sealed quotation method can be used for procurement of works, goods, and services alike - so all of the above can be procured.

q: 16. The money of the contractor retained by the department during payments is called :
explain: Retention money is a percentage withheld from progress payments to ensure the contractor completes the work and fixes defects.

q: 17. Generally in GoN office, what is the main intention of Office Chief
explain: While bidding is the legal standard, office chiefs often prefer direct purchase for smaller, urgent requirements due to speed.

q: 18. The opening of bidding in the process of procurement is
explain: Tendering opens the bidding process.

q: 19. The amount of VAT for the purchase of steel having an amount of NRs. 6000/- should be
explain: VAT in Nepal is 13%. $6000 \times 0.13 = 780$.

q: 20. The authority of Gazetted third officer for the approval of estimate is (Source:PPR 2064(14))
explain: Based on the Public Procurement Rules of Nepal, a 3rd class gazetted officer has an approval limit under 50 million.

q: 21. The minimum no. of parties for doing any contract/agreement should be
explain: A contract requires a minimum of two parties: the promisor and the promisee.

q: 22. The various types of contract are
explain: These are all standard methods of contracting used in the construction industry.

q: 23. The amount of money paid to the contractor by the client after the agreement and before the execution of work, is known as
explain: Mobilization advance is an advance payment made to the contractor after signing the agreement to help setup initial site operations and resources.

q: 24. The increase in price of materials during the construction is called
explain: Price escalation clauses allow for cost adjustments if material/labor prices rise significantly during the project.

q: 25. The main criteria for the selection of any contractor to perform any work are
explain: Contractors are evaluated on their financial stability, technical skill, available machinery, and past performance.

q: 26. The price adjustment clause is essential for contract having duration greater than ……… months.
explain: Per the answer key, 12 months.

q: 27. The document announcing to prospective bidders that the owner is ready to receive bids is called
explain: A 'notice to bidders' (or tender notice) is the document that announces the owner's readiness to receive bids from prospective bidders.

q: 28. FIDIC is
explain: FIDIC stands for the International Federation of Consulting Engineers, known for its standard contract forms.

q: 29. The earnest money deposited by unsuccessful bidder is returned after
explain: Per the answer key, after the contract is awarded to the successful bidder.

q: 30. *Acquisition of land for any construction should be performed :
explain: The owner must have possession of the land before inviting contractors to bid to avoid delays and legal issues.

q: 31. The penalty provision in any contract agreement is
explain: Per the answer key, 0.05% per day.

q: 32. Contractor's prequalification is required for project cost above (Source: PPR2064(3))
explain: Under Public Procurement Regulations (PPR 2064, Rule 3), mandatory pre-qualification is specified for large projects exceeding threshold values.

q: 33. The railway projects are treated as
explain: Railway construction involves massive earthworks and heavy infrastructure, placing it in the heavy construction category.

q: 34. The relation between contractor and client should be
explain: A healthy project environment requires both clear decision-making and a cooperative attitude between the owner and the builder.

q: 35. Force Majeure in a contract is:
options: Occurrence of an act beyond the control of both the parties in contract agreement
Preventing both parties to perform the respective obligation agreed
explain: Force majeure encompasses both the occurrence of an uncontrollable event and its effect of preventing both parties from performing their obligations - both A and B.

q: 36. Acquisition of land for any construction should be perfomed :
explain: To prevent site possession disputes and contract delays, land acquisition and right-of-way clearances must be secured prior to issuing tender notices.

q: 37. An EPC contract means:
explain: EPC stands for Engineering, Procurement, and Construction—a form of turnkey agreement where one contractor handles total delivery.

q: 38. The supplementary specification prepared and applied if the standard specification does not cover the requirement of works under a contract is called:
explain: The answer key indicates 'performance specification', though in many contexts, these are also referred to as 'special specifications'.

q: 39. The main criteria for selection of contractors to execute work is
explain: Per the answer key, all of these.

q: 40. Best option to avoid the undue pressure, cartels and collusion during bidding process is
explain: Per the answer key, e-bidding, which removes face-to-face contact between bidders and officials.

q: 41. A contractor's role in construction includes:
explain: Maintaining safety at the construction site is a core responsibility of the contractor, unlike payment/certification which are the client/engineer's roles.

q: 42. Earnest money is a ........ towards the execution of a publicly tender government contract.
explain: Earnest money is a security deposit made to guarantee bid commitment during public tender procedures.

q: 43. The document giving the information about the tender, prequalification, contractor, construction, procurement of materials and services is called
explain: The tender document (or bid document) contains all the necessary information for a contractor to prepare a bid.

q: 44. "Fraudulent Practice" means
options: The offering, giving, receiving of anything of value of influence the action of a public official in the procurement process
Misrepresentation of facts to influence a procurement process
explain: Fraudulent practice covers both improper inducement of officials and misrepresentation of facts - both a and b.

q: 45. The contractor shall submit an application to the employer for extension of time, stating the causes for delay, ……… days before the expiry of contract completion date.
explain: The number of days is missing from the printed stem. Per the key, 21 days.

q: 46. The employer shall pay the interim bill within ……… days after the bill submitted by the contractor.
explain: Per the answer key, 30 days.

q: 47. Time extension may need to be granted due to
explain: Time extensions can be warranted by force majeure events as well as delays caused by the purchaser/employer - both a and b.

q: 48. The purpose of bid evaluation is to evaluate
explain: Evaluation identifies the lowest evaluated substantially responsive bidder.

q: 49. The remuneration of dispute adjudication board is paid by
explain: The client and contractor share the cost.

q: 50. A contractor can start the construction works with following the receipt of
explain: The 'notice to proceed' is the formal authorization document that allows the contractor to commence construction works.
